hunks.baseline: At that moment, there was only one thought in the black-robed man’s mind.
hunks.sol: At that moment, only one thought ran through the black-robed man’s mind.

hunks.baseline: It was a perfectly reasonable question for him to ask himself.
hunks.sol: It was a reasonable question.

hunks.baseline: He was a sorcerer.
A highly experienced one, with considerable skill.
hunks.sol: He was a sorcerer. An experienced one, and highly skilled.

hunks.baseline: He had neither internal energy measured in jiazi nor martial arts exceptional enough to be called divine. But he did have the ability to control hundreds of monsters perfectly.
hunks.sol: He had neither internal energy measured in jiazi nor martial arts exceptional enough to be called divine. What he did have was the ability to control hundreds of monsters perfectly.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man stared blankly at the monster before him—or, more precisely, at the uninvited guest who had obviously pulled a monster’s hide over himself.
hunks.sol: He stared blankly at the monster before him—or rather, at the intruder who had clearly pulled a monster’s hide over himself.

hunks.baseline: Only after pinching his arm hard enough to confirm he wasn’t dreaming could he finally squeeze out the question he’d been holding back.
hunks.sol: Only after pinching his arm hard enough to confirm he wasn’t dreaming could he force out the question he’d been holding back.

hunks.baseline: The mysterious intruder flinched and answered in a halting voice.
hunks.sol: The intruder flinched and answered haltingly.

hunks.baseline: “……You’re talking like a person.”
hunks.sol: “…You’re talking like a person.”

hunks.baseline: “……There can’t be.”
hunks.sol: “…No, there aren’t.”

hunks.baseline: At the black-robed man’s thoroughly logical rebuttal, delivered with all the confidence of an expert, the intruder fell silent for a moment, then opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: Faced with the expert’s thoroughly logical rebuttal, the intruder fell silent for a moment. Then he opened his mouth.

hunks.baseline: The intruder kept making uncertain monster noises, now raising both arms like a jiangshi. The black-robed man sank into even greater confusion and shouted.
hunks.sol: Now he was even raising both arms like a jiangshi as he continued his uncertain attempts at a monster’s roar. The black-robed man, more confused than ever, shouted, “Stop!”

hunks.baseline: “Stop!”
“Gasp. Why?”
hunks.sol: The intruder gasped. “Why?”

hunks.baseline: “What the hell is this supposed to be?”
hunks.sol: “What the hell are you doing?”

hunks.baseline: “I was doing my best to imitate them… Wasn’t that last one pretty close?”
hunks.sol: “I was trying my best to imitate them… Wasn’t that last one pretty close?”

hunks.baseline: “No, that one was a little close.”
hunks.sol: “Well, the last one was a little close.”

hunks.baseline: “Wow! I knew it! Thank you!”
hunks.sol: “Wow, I knew it! Thank you!”

hunks.baseline: An exchange that strayed far enough from common sense could paralyze the mind.
hunks.sol: An exchange that strayed this far from common sense could paralyze the mind.

hunks.baseline: Just as the black-robed man ran out of words, the intruder, unable to hide his delight, added proudly:
“All that practice for two days straight paid off. I guess it’s true what they say: hard work doesn’t betray you.”
hunks.sol: While the black-robed man struggled for words, the intruder added proudly, unable to hide his delight, “All that practice for two days straight paid off. Grandpa was right—hard work doesn’t betray you.”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man, still floundering in confusion, blinked at the unexpected answer.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man blinked, still floundering in confusion.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, that hard work doesn’t betray you? My grandfather’s been telling me that since I was little…”
hunks.sol: “Oh, about hard work not betraying you? My grandfather’s been telling me that since I was little…”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, I know what you mean. The big people. Well, it’s not quite right to call them people, but anyway, I hid in there and kept trying to imitate them.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, I know what you mean. The big people. Well, I guess it’s not quite right to call them people, but anyway, I hid among them and kept practicing.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. Like I said before, I’ve been doing it for two days.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. Like I said, I’ve been doing it for two days.”

hunks.baseline: Despite the intruder’s innocent answer, the black-robed man was struck by a shock that seemed to freeze his spine.
hunks.sol: The answer was innocent enough, but the black-robed man felt a shock run down his spine.

hunks.baseline: After grueling training, he’d gained the ability to perfectly control some five hundred monsters. That was why he could detect the life energy of living humans with his eyes closed.
hunks.sol: After grueling training, he’d gained the ability to control some five hundred monsters perfectly. He could detect the life energy of a living human with his eyes closed.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man sensed it instinctively.
Every word the mysterious intruder before him had spoken was true—not a single one a lie.
hunks.sol: He could feel it instinctively. Everything the intruder had said was true, without a single lie.

hunks.baseline: As far as he could tell, the man didn’t have the Intelligence to lie convincingly. And now that he’d been caught so plainly, he had no reason to hide anything.
hunks.sol: As far as the black-robed man could tell, the fellow wasn’t intelligent enough to lie convincingly. And after being caught so plainly, he had no reason to keep anything hidden.

hunks.baseline: Those thoughts, and the situation unfolding around him, finally helped the black-robed man come to his senses, as if he’d been bewitched.
hunks.sol: That realization finally brought the black-robed man to his senses. Until now, he might as well have been bewitched.

hunks.baseline: “Shut up, you lunatic.”
hunks.sol: “Shut up, you madman.”

hunks.baseline: “Lunatic? That’s a very vulgar and bad word. My grandfather told me never to say it.”
hunks.sol: “Madman? That’s a very vulgar and bad word. My grandfather told me never to say it.”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man felt his blood rushing to his head.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man felt his blood rush to his head. However unexpected the situation, he’d let this lunatic play him, if only for a moment.

hunks.baseline: Even if the situation had caught him completely off guard, he’d let himself be played by some lunatic, if only for a moment.
He shook the evil bell in his hand, his anger lending force to the motion.
hunks.sol: He shook the evil bell in his hand, putting all his anger into the motion.

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t his imagination. There was unusual force behind the bell’s sound.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t imagined the extra force in its sound.

hunks.baseline: The distinctive death energy possessed only by sorcerers who commanded monsters made the sound more ominous and clear. That chilling tone carried two meanings.
hunks.sol: The death energy possessed by sorcerers who commanded monsters made the ringing clearer and more sinister. That chilling note carried two messages.

hunks.baseline: First: alert the other sorcerers stationed nearby to the situation.
hunks.sol: First, it alerted the other sorcerers stationed nearby to what was happening.

hunks.baseline: Leave the disposal of that lunatic to the hundred or so monsters he’d brought as guards.
hunks.sol: It ordered the hundred or so monsters he’d brought as guards to deal with the madman.

hunks.baseline: The monsters swept around them with speed that belied their enormous frames, forming an impenetrable wall in front of the black-robed man. From behind it, he spoke through clenched teeth.
hunks.sol: The monsters swept around them with speed that belied their enormous frames, surrounding the intruder and forming an iron wall in front of the black-robed man. From behind it, he ground out his offer.

hunks.baseline: “If you surrender quietly right now and tell me everything you know, I’ll promise you a relatively quick and painless death.”
hunks.sol: “Surrender quietly and tell me everything you know. I’ll give you a relatively quick and painless death.”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man wasn’t relying on numbers alone.
hunks.sol: He wasn’t relying on numbers alone.

hunks.baseline: Each monster guarding him had skill comparable to a master ranging from at least Supreme First Rate up to Peak.

hunks.sol: Each of his guards had power comparable to a master somewhere between Supreme First Rate and Peak. Their strength and speed surpassed human limits, and their tenacious vitality was the stuff of nightmares.

hunks.baseline: Even if the intruder before him was a lunatic with tremendous skill, the outcome wouldn’t change in the slightest.
hunks.sol: Even if the lunatic before him possessed tremendous skill, the black-robed man was certain the outcome wouldn’t change. The intruder had more than these monsters to contend with.

hunks.baseline: The monsters here weren’t the only ones he’d have to face.
“Go ahead and struggle all you want. You won’t even be able to do that a few moments from now.”
hunks.sol: “Struggle all you like. In a few moments, you won’t even be able to do that.”

hunks.sol: Thinking of his fellow sorcerers, who should have received the signal and be rushing here already, the black-robed man curled one corner of his mouth.

hunks.baseline: “But why haven’t I gotten a reply?”
hunks.sol: “But why haven’t they answered?”

hunks.sol: The intruder’s sudden question caught him off guard.

hunks.baseline: “A reply. Uh, in this case, should I call it a reply-sound? Anyway, from what I’ve seen over the past two days, you always communicate with the bell, even over the smallest things.”
hunks.sol: “Answered. Uh, should I call it an answering ring? Anyway, I watched you for two days. You always send a bell signal back, even for the smallest thing.”
“…Huh?”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man suddenly realized something. He hurriedly looked around.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man looked around in a hurry.

hunks.baseline: No—he focused all his attention on listening.
He was waiting to hear his fellow sorcerers answer, their sinister bell sounds similar to his own.
hunks.sol: No. Looking would do him no good. He focused every bit of his attention on listening for his fellow sorcerers’ reply—for the sinister ringing of bells like his own.

hunks.baseline: But the only sounds reaching his ears were the wind blowing from far away and the breathing of the monsters surrounding them. Nothing answered.
hunks.sol: But all he heard was the wind blowing in from far away and the breathing of the monsters around him. No answer came.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man’s heart lurched.
hunks.sol: His heart lurched.

hunks.baseline: Something had gone wrong.
hunks.sol: Something was wrong. Terribly wrong.

hunks.baseline: Terribly wrong.
With a sense of foreboding sweeping through his mind, his confused eyes turned toward one figure.
The intruder, surrounded by horrible monsters, had perked up his ears and even cupped his hands around them like a trumpet to listen.
hunks.sol: As dread swept through him, his eyes turned toward the intruder. Despite being surrounded by monsters, the fellow had his ears pricked and his hands cupped around them like a trumpet, listening too.

hunks.baseline: “Oh. You’re right. I can’t hear anything. Nothing at all.”
hunks.sol: “Oh. I really can’t hear them. Nothing at all.”

hunks.baseline: “You, you…”
hunks.sol: “You… You…”

hunks.baseline: What was he supposed to say?
hunks.sol: What could he say? How was he supposed to make sense of this?

hunks.baseline: How could he make sense of this situation?
The black-robed man could barely get the words out. Beyond the discolored monster hide, the intruder’s eyes curved clearly into crescents.
hunks.sol: He couldn’t even form the words. Beyond the discolored hide, he saw the intruder’s eyes curve into crescents.

hunks.baseline: “L-Little Grandpa?”
hunks.sol: “Little… Grandpa?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. He’s the one who teaches me all sorts of things. He gets really angry whenever I call him Little Grandpa, but sometimes it seems like he secretly likes it, too.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. He teaches me all sorts of things. He gets really angry whenever I call him Little Grandpa, but sometimes I think he secretly likes it, too.”

hunks.baseline: The intruder stopped rambling and snapped his mouth shut with a little gasp.
hunks.sol: The intruder caught himself rambling and snapped his mouth shut with a gasp.

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man didn’t answer.
More precisely, he no longer had the presence of mind to answer.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man didn’t answer. He no longer had the presence of mind to.

hunks.baseline: He could only stare blankly at the intruder, who had finally stopped talking, then squeeze out the question that had just come to mind.
hunks.sol: He stared at the intruder, who had finally stopped talking, and barely managed to force out the question that had just come to him.

hunks.baseline: “Who… No, who are you people?”
hunks.sol: “Who are you…? No, who are you people?”

hunks.baseline: His vision was blurring. The words he’d just heard had made him realize a truth he desperately didn’t want to believe.
hunks.sol: His vision swam. What he’d just heard had made him realize a truth he desperately didn’t want to believe.

hunks.baseline: The other thirty or so sorcerers who’d come here with him were already dead.
hunks.sol: The other thirty or so sorcerers who had come here with him were already dead.

hunks.baseline: They’d been killed the same way the intruder had slipped in beside him—or in a manner even more secretive and deadly.
hunks.sol: Perhaps their killers had slipped close the way this intruder had. Perhaps they’d used methods even quieter and deadlier.

hunks.baseline: Even if anyone was still alive, they wouldn’t be for long.
hunks.sol: If any were still alive, they wouldn’t be for long.

hunks.baseline: If the owner of the sobriquet that had just flashed through the black-robed man’s mind was here now…
hunks.sol: Not if the man whose sobriquet had just flashed through the black-robed man’s mind was here.

hunks.baseline: “Th-that Little Grandpa of yours—could it be…?”
hunks.sol: “Th-that Little Grandpa of yours… Don’t tell me he’s…”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man’s voice trailed off. Then—
The flat voice suddenly pierced his ears, and a shock like lightning striking the crown of his head swept over him.
hunks.sol: The emotionless voice pierced his ears. Shock struck him like lightning through the crown of his head.

hunks.baseline: Little Grandpa—no, *that man.*
hunks.sol: Little Grandpa—no, *that man*.

hunks.baseline: And yet he hadn’t sensed the man’s breathing. He hadn’t detected the breath that should have brushed the back of his neck along with the voice—not even the slightest trace of presence or life energy.
hunks.sol: Yet the black-robed man hadn’t sensed his breathing. No breath had brushed the back of his neck when the man spoke. He’d detected neither the slightest presence nor a trace of life energy.

hunks.baseline: The breathless voice sounded again in the black-robed man’s ear, whose body had gone rigid as a statue.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man stood rigid as a statue. The breathless voice came again.

hunks.baseline: “I asked you. What the hell did you say?”
hunks.sol: “I asked you. What were you babbling about?”

hunks.baseline: He could only make one last desperate attempt—the instinctive final struggle to survive.
hunks.sol: All he could do was make one final, instinctive struggle to survive.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t even realize that a thin line had cut across his wrist before he could move the old, bloodstained evil bell, which was practically everything he had.
hunks.sol: He didn’t even realize a line had crossed his wrist before he could move the old, bloodstained evil bell that was practically everything he had.

hunks.baseline: Everything happened a moment too late.
hunks.sol: Everything came a moment too late.

hunks.baseline: The wrist, severed from its owner, hit the ground. Its owner noticed it only after it was gone.
hunks.sol: The severed wrist hit the ground. Only then did its owner notice it was gone.

hunks.baseline: And the black-robed man recognized the pain only when it arrived at last, then let out a scream filled with fear.
hunks.sol: The pain arrived last. The black-robed man felt it and tried to scream in terror.

hunks.baseline: *Thump. Collapse.*
hunks.sol: *Tap. Thud.*

hunks.baseline: His body crumpled helplessly as the Sleep Acupoint was pressed.
hunks.sol: His Sleep Acupoint was pressed, and his body crumpled helplessly.

hunks.baseline: And so the black-robed man plunged into a pitch-black abyss with no end in sight, unable even to scream properly.
hunks.sol: Unable even to finish his scream, he plunged into pitch-black darkness with no end in sight. The voices of two people drifted after him, faint as a dream.

hunks.baseline: Behind him, the voices of two people sounded distant and dreamlike.
“……This is driving me crazy. Let’s go find that guy.”
hunks.sol: “…You’re driving me insane. Let’s go find that guy.”

hunks.baseline: Truly, right to the very end, it was like a nightmare.
hunks.sol: Right to the very end, it was a nightmare.
